competitors.name: Microsoft Power Query (Excel / Power BI)
competitors.notes: Built into Excel and Power BI. Can combine multiple files from a folder, but requires manual schema mapping (promote headers, change types, merge queries). Not fully automatic when column names or order change. Free with Excel.
competitors.feature_overlap: Combines multiple Excel/CSV files, supports transformations, refreshable queries.
competitors.pricing: Free with Excel 2016+ or Power BI Desktop
competitors.market_positioning: Standard data preparation tool for Microsoft ecosystem

competitors.name: Alteryx Designer
competitors.notes: Enterprise data preparation platform. Can automatically combine files with different schemas using 'Auto Field' and 'Union' tools. Handles schema drift. Very powerful but expensive and requires training.
competitors.feature_overlap: Full data blending, merging, schema alignment, automation.
competitors.market_positioning: Premium data analytics automation for enterprises

competitors.name: Easy Data Transform
competitors.notes: Desktop tool for merging CSV/Excel files. Can combine files with different columns using 'Merge' operation. Simple UI but still requires manual column mapping. One-time purchase.
competitors.feature_overlap: Merge multiple files, transform columns, export.

competitors.name: CSV Merge (various online tools)
competitors.notes: Simple online tools to merge CSV files. Usually require same columns or manual selection. No handling of different schemas. Free but limited.
competitors.feature_overlap: Basic merging of CSV files with same structure.

competitors.name: OpenRefine
competitors.notes: Open-source data cleaning tool. Can import multiple files, reconcile columns, and merge datasets. Requires manual steps and some learning. Not automatic.
competitors.market_positioning: Open-source data wrangling for power users

competitors.name: Python (pandas) / R (dplyr)
competitors.notes: Scripting libraries for data manipulation. Can automate merging with code, but requires programming skills. Not a SaaS product.
competitors.feature_overlap: Full control over merging, schema mapping via code.

competitors.name: Tableau Prep Builder
competitors.notes: Data preparation tool from Tableau. Can combine files, but schema mapping is manual. Visual interface. Part of Tableau ecosystem.

competitors.name: Google Sheets (IMPORTRANGE + QUERY)
competitors.notes: Can import data from other sheets and combine using formulas. Manual setup, breaks with schema changes. Free with Google account.

competitors.name: Zapier / Make (Integromat)
competitors.notes: Automation platforms that can move data between apps. Can combine files via steps, but not designed for complex schema merging. Requires manual mapping.

competitors.name: Talend Data Preparation
competitors.notes: Cloud data preparation tool. Can combine datasets, but schema mapping is manual. Free version available.
competitors.market_positioning: Enterprise data integration with prep capabilities

competitors.name: Knime Analytics Platform
competitors.notes: Open-source data analytics platform. Can merge files with nodes, but requires visual workflow building and manual mapping. Free.

summary: The competitive landscape for merging Excel/CSV files with different schemas is moderately crowded. Established tools like Power Query (free, built-in), Alteryx (powerful but expensive), and open-source options (Python, OpenRefine) exist. However, nearly all require manual schema mapping, scripting, or significant training. No single product offers a truly automatic, no-code, affordable solution that handles arbitrary column differences without user intervention. This gap represents an opportunity, but the presence of many partial alternatives means the market is not empty. Competition score is 3: established alternatives exist, but none perfectly solve the core pain point of automatic schema alignment.
